chunks: We do not come down but only by your Lord's command. To Him belongs whatever lies before us and behind us, and the space in between. Your Lord does not ever forget:

key_terms.بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ: By the command of your Lord
key_terms.نَتَنَزَّلُ: We descend (angels coming down to earth)
key_terms.نَسِيًّا: Forgetful / One who does not forget

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of angels descending by God's command in Surah Maryam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the absolute obedience of the angels, particularly Gabriel, who descend not by independent will but solely by divine decree, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid in action. It serves as a counterpoint to the disbelievers' claim that angels are independent deities, highlighting that all realms—past, present, and future—are under God's complete surveillance and memory. This emphasizes that divine communication is a deliberate, commanded act rather than a spontaneous occurrence.
